reviews.title: great game
reviews.text: its an addictive and straightforward game where you manage and grow a mining empire. Overall, it’s a fun and engaging way to pass the time, particularly if you enjoy management games.

reviews.title: Pay to win
reviews.text:

 But if you want to play the events you will have to spend a lot of money. 24 hours of a x2 buff, 12 plus hour of a x10 and a few x20 mix with instant coin reward buff and 3,000 super cash later and I am still not able to win an event. The events are so rigged. You can see the difference between your normal mines and event mines. Regular your elevator and bank can be a few level difference but in events your elevator has to be 20 levels higher then bank or your not making any progress. Plus the cost is outrageously high to normal game play and the income is greatly reduced. So if you start a regular mine and event mine at the same time your regular mine would max out 5x faster then event mine.

reviews.title: New Features:  Give us all your money, arrrrbghhhh!!
reviews.text:
The devs have lost their ever-loving minds.  Every single minute change to this game is geared specifically to screw the player into spending ever-increasing amounts of money, essentially for the experience of playing a spreadsheet with mediocre graphics.  

The art in the game is appallingly bad, which could be forgiven early on in the game’s uninspired and bland history.  The gameplay itself involves little more than watching numbers as they crawl their way to ever higher exponents, which themselves are expressed as letters, in case scientific notation wasn’t taught in your public school system.
